post.summary: `POST /admin/refresh` — operator-triggered reconciler tick.
post.description:
Audit: writes [`audit::ADMIN_REFRESH`] with target
`"scope:all"`, `"org:<id>"`, or `"org:<id>;repo:<id>"`. The row
lands even on coalesce — the operator's *intent* is what we
audit, not whether a tick physically ran.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Narrow the tick to one org

parameters.name: repo_id
parameters.description: Narrow the tick to one repo (requires org_id)

get.summary: `GET /admin/runs` — paginated `dp_fetch_runs` projection.

post.summary: `POST /admin/users/:id/anonymise` — irreversible GDPR cascade.
post.description:
Calls [`Store::pseudonymise_user`], which rewrites
`login`/`email`/`name` to a `deleted-user-<short>` form and sets
`deleted_at`. The row id is preserved so historical reports
keep referential integrity (§0.5).

Audit: writes [`audit::USER_ANONYMISE`], target
`"user:<id>"`, **after** the cascade succeeds — a failed
cascade does not leave a misleading audit trail.

get.summary:
`GET /admin/users/:id/export` — chunked JSON dump of every row
dev-pulse holds about the user.
get.description:
Wire shape: a single JSON object matching [`UserExport`]. We
emit it incrementally so the process never holds more than one
page of event rows in memory at a time:

1. `{"user":<user>,"memberships":<memberships>,"events":[`
2. one JSON object per event, comma-separated, page by page
3. `]}`

Audit: writes [`audit::USER_EXPORT`], target `"user:<id>"`,
**before** streaming starts. Auditing pre-stream is deliberate
— the request was authorised, so the access attempt should be
recorded even if the network drops mid-stream.

post.summary: `POST /home-org` — atomically flip the user's home org.
post.description:
Postcondition (enforced by [`Store::set_home_org_for_user`]):
exactly one membership row per `user_id` has `home_org =
Some(org_id)` after this call returns.

Audit: writes one [`audit::HOME_ORG_SET`] row, `target =
"user:<user_id>"`. The row is written **after** the store flip
succeeds so a failed mutation doesn't leave a misleading audit
trail.

[`Store::set_home_org_for_user`]: dp_domain::store::Store::set_home_org_for_user

get.summary:
`GET /issues` — paginated, filterable issue list. Ordered by
`updated_at DESC` (matches GitHub's default "recently updated"
view).

post.summary: `POST /issues` — create a new GitHub issue.
post.description:
No CAS on the issue itself (there is no local row yet). Sequence:

1. Resolve `repo_id -> (Org, Repo)`.
2. §18.2 step 4 install-permission check.
3. Call the backend's `create_issue`. On success the backend
   returns the GitHub issue payload, which we hand to
   [`dp_fetcher::worker::handlers::parse_issue_upsert`] +
   [`Store::upsert_issue_from_github`] to materialise the local
   `dp_issues` row immediately — same two-way-sync trick the
   PATCH handler uses.
4. Optional attach: when `project_id` is set, attach the new
   issue to that project (and to `view_id`'s membership table
   when set), reusing the same semantics as
   [`crate::project_issues::bulk_add_issues`]:
   * `project_id` only → project-level add, requires
     `expected_version` (`400 missing_expected_version` if not
     supplied), bumps project version.
   * `project_id` + `view_id` → view-membership only; no CAS,
     no project version bump.
5. Record the `issue.create` audit row (target =
   `repo_id#number`, with `:project=…` / `:view=…` suffixes
   when the attach paths fired).

400.description: Validation failed at GitHub, or missing expected_version

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

404.description: Project id supplied but project does not exist

get.summary: `GET /issues/{id}` — single issue by id.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /issues/{id}` — update an existing GitHub issue. Routes
the `state` transition (open/closed) to the `issue.close` /
`issue.reopen` audit verbs; everything else is `issue.update`.

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

409.description: Stale local version — UI should reload

post.summary:
`POST /issues/{id}/comments` — append a comment. CAS-gated for
symmetry with PATCH so the UI's optimistic editor sees the same
stale-version surface.
post.description:
After the GitHub call lands we do a best-effort single-issue
refetch (`gh_get_issue`) and project the payload through
`parse_issue_upsert`, so the local row's `comment_count` /
`updated_at` advance synchronously — without this the UI saw
the post-comment row stuck at the pre-write count until the
next webhook / reconciler tick (the bug the user reported).
The response carries the fresh `IssueDto` for the same reason
the PATCH handler does.

200.description: Comment posted; fresh issue row returned

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

409.description: Stale local version — UI should reload

get.summary:
`GET /issues/{id}/dates` — read the local `dp_issue_dates` row
for an issue. Returns `200 { issue_id, start_at: null, due_at:
null, … }` with all nullable fields set when no row exists, so
the frontend can render the picker uniformly. Authorisation:
the same `(issues, read)` pair the rest of the read surface uses
— read-only and per-org, the picker is also visible to viewers
who cannot write.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /issues/{id}/dates` — see module docs for the four-step
shape. Authorisation: `(issues, write)`.

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

get.summary:
`GET /issues/{id}/project` — resolve the (single, per v1 `UNIQUE
(issue_id)`) project for an issue, or `null` when the issue is
not in any project. Backs the §6.5 detail-pane chip.

post.summary:
`POST /issues/{id}/refresh` — fire-and-forget single-issue
resync the UI calls when an issue is opened (or when the user
hits a "refresh" affordance). Performs a `GET
/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}` against GitHub, projects
the payload through `parse_issue_upsert`, and returns the post-
upsert row — so the frontend can swap its cached row for the
fresh one in a single round-trip.
post.description:
Gated on `(issues, read)`: refreshing a row is a read of the
underlying issue (no GitHub mutation happens). The backend may
return `None` (the unconfigured stub, test fakes) in which case
we simply re-read the local row and return it — callers get a
200 with the existing state, never a 503, so the lazy-refresh
effect on the frontend is safe to fire unconditionally.

200.description: Refreshed (or fell back to local row when no backend is configured)

get.summary:
`GET /issues/{id}/timeline` — newest-first activity strip for
one issue. The lookup uses the §6 guarded expression index on
`dp_activity_events` so the predicate is index-only even when
the parent repo has decades of accumulated history.

`GET /me/app-install-banner` — the §13.6 one-shot migration
banner data for the caller.
get.description:
* Reads memberships through `Store::list_memberships_for_user`
  so the §15.11 access gate is the only visibility check
  (out-of-org users get an empty `orgs` list — same as the
  `/orgs` directory surface).
* Per-org `writes_available` is the *same* verdict
  [`require_issues_write`] would return — no separate code
  path, no risk of the banner saying "you can write" while the
  write-gate disagrees.
* Not audited (read-only, no mutation).

200.description: Per-org App install status + §13.6 admin copy text

get.summary: `GET /me/identities`.

200.description: Linked OAuth identities for the caller

503.description: Identity store not wired in this deployment

post.summary:
`POST /me/inbox/bulk` — bulk inbox transitions
(mark-all-seen / snooze-all / done-all / inbox-all). Used by the
list-header bulk action menu in the workbench. Audited under the
`BULK_INBOX_*` vocabulary so the audit log can answer "who did
the mass dismiss?" without scanning the per-row writes.

400.description: Batch too large / snooze without deadline

post.summary:
`POST /me/inbox/seen` — bulk-mark issues read. Idempotent. The
store upserts one `dp_user_issue_state` row per id, setting
`last_seen_version` from `dp_issues.version` (so the UI never
has to know the version itself).

400.description: Too many issue ids in one batch

patch.description:
The body's `status` and `snoozed_until` are written verbatim;
see [`SetInboxStateRequest`] for the consistency contract.

Returns the resulting row so the UI can confirm without a
second round-trip.

get.summary: `GET /me/orgs` — orgs the caller has a membership in.
get.description:
Narrower than `GET /orgs` (which returns every org dev-pulse
has observed). Use this surface when the UI needs to scope a
write to an org the caller is allowed to write to — e.g. the
Account → Tags page picking a scope for `POST /tags`, whose
backend gate (`tags::ViewerVisibility::visible_org_ids`) only
admits orgs the caller is a direct member of. Returning the
full directory there causes a confusing 403 when the operator
picks an org they can see but isn't in.

200.description: Orgs the caller is a member of

get.summary: `GET /me/pins` — caller's pins, ordered by `position` ascending.
get.description:
Audit: not audited. Pins are personal UI state and `GET` traffic
would swamp the audit log without operational value (§6.5 only
pins the three mutation verbs).

post.summary: `POST /me/pins` — append a pin to the caller's list.
post.description:
* Position is server-assigned (`len(existing)`).
* Returns `400 pin_cap_exceeded` if the caller already has
  [`PIN_CAP`] pins (§13.5).
* Returns `409 pin_exists` if the `(kind, target_id)` row is
  already in the caller's pins (idempotent re-pinning, §6.4 /
  the composite-PK note in [`dp_domain::store::Store::add_pin`]).
* Audit: writes [`audit::PIN_ADD`] with target
  `"<kind>:<target_id>"` after the row lands.

409.description: Pin already exists for this caller

put.summary: `PUT /me/pins/order` — atomically rewrite the caller's pin order.
put.description:
The request body's `order` must exactly cover the caller's
current pin set; missing or extra `(kind, target_id)` entries
surface as `400 reorder_set_mismatch`. The store applies the
rewrite in one transaction so a concurrent reader cannot observe
a partial reorder (§6.3 row-by-row comment, §13 atomicity rules).

Audit: writes one [`audit::PIN_REORDER`] row with target
`"count:<n>"` (n = number of pins reordered). We do **not** dump
the full key list into the audit target — that would balloon the
`dp_audit_log.target` column past the small-text comfort zone
and the audit verb is meaningful at row granularity (one row =
one reorder operation).

400.description: `order` does not exactly cover the caller's pins

delete.description:
Returns `404 pin_not_found` when the row is not in the caller's
pin set. Audit: writes [`audit::PIN_REMOVE`] after the row is
gone.

Note on positions: the §6.3 schema does not auto-compact `position`
values on delete (the store does not renumber). The next
[`reorder_pins`](crate::pins::reorder_pins) call is what compacts
the gap.

get.summary:
`GET /me/queue` — the caller's inbox. The default landing view
for the triage page (`linear-projects-idea.md` §3.8 / §5.4).
get.description:
Returns issues that the caller has not dismissed (`status <>
'done'`) and that are not currently snoozed (`status <>
'snoozed' OR snoozed_until < now()`). Rows that have never
been touched surface as default-state ("inbox", unread until
the user opens the peek panel).

Accepts the same filter set as `GET /issues` so the smart-view
rail can pre-narrow ("My queue · phoenix only", etc.).

Each row carries an `unread` boolean — `true` when
`dp_issues.version > last_seen_version`. The frontend renders
an indicator and uses `POST /me/inbox/seen` to clear it when
the user opens the row in the peek panel.

parameters.name: untriaged
parameters.description: Restrict to rows with no assignee and no label

get.summary:
`GET /me/settings` — list every catalogue entry, joined with
the caller's row when one exists.
get.description:
Returns one [`SettingDto`] per entry in [`KEYS`] (not per
row) so the frontend can render the full settings form even
for a brand-new user with zero saved settings. Secret values
are always redacted (see [`SettingDto::value`]).

post.summary:
`POST /me/settings/github.pat/test` — call `GET /user` on
github.com with the caller's stored PAT and report the
outcome. Diagnostic only; does not store or surface the
token value back to the caller. Returns `200` for both
success and failure outcomes so the UI can switch on the
`ok` discriminator instead of catching errors.

get.summary: `GET /me/settings/{key}` — fetch a single setting.
get.description:
Returns `400 unknown_setting` for keys not in [`KEYS`] and
a [`SettingDto`] with `has_value: false` for known-but-unset
keys (i.e. *not* a 404 — the catalogue entry always exists).

400.description: Key not in the pinned catalogue

put.description:
Returns `400 unknown_setting` for keys not in [`KEYS`]. The
response is the post-write [`SettingDto`] (with redaction
applied for secret keys, so the UI can confirm "set" without
ever receiving the value back).

Audit: writes [`audit::SETTING_SET`] with target = the key
(never the value).

400.description: Key not in the pinned catalogue

delete.description:
Returns `400 unknown_setting` for keys not in [`KEYS`] and
`404 setting_unset` when the key is known but no row exists.

Audit: writes [`audit::SETTING_DELETE`] with target = the key.

400.description: Key not in the pinned catalogue

404.description: Key is known but no row exists for the caller

get.summary: `GET /me/tags` — caller-owned or caller-is-scope-member tags.
get.description:
Convenience over `GET /tags` for the new-tag picker and the
"my tags" sidebar group. Returns the same row shape; the
filter is "the viewer is a scope member" (which for user-scope
= owner, for team/org-scope = membership).

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description: Include archived tags in the response. Default `false`.

200.description: Tags caller owns or is a scope member of

get.summary:
`GET /orgs` — every org dev-pulse has observed. (Stage 9 will
narrow to "orgs the principal can see"; stage 4 returns all.)

`GET /orgs/{org_id}/projects-v2` — normalized board picker for
the §6.4 link dialog. Returns 503 when no picker backend is
wired (the UI then renders an `[Open GitHub project settings]`
hint per §6.4); the empty-result case is `200 { boards: [],
fetched_at }` so the UI can distinguish "no boards" from
"transport down".
`GET /projects` — filtered, paginated list.
get.description:
* Defaults to `limit = 50`, capped at `MAX_LIST_LIMIT = 200`.
* Pass `?count_only=1` for an empty-`rows` count-only envelope
  (§6.1 sidebar).
* Order: status (active → backlog → done → archived) then
  `due_at ASC NULLS LAST` then `name`.

parameters.name: count_only
parameters.description: If 1, returns count only with empty rows.

post.summary:
`POST /projects` — create. Initialises `version = 1`,
`issue_count = closed_issue_count = 0`, stamps `created_by`
from the [`Principal`]. Audits [`audit::PROJECT_CREATE`].

409.description: Duplicate active project name in this org

get.summary: `GET /projects/{id}` — single project, or `404` when absent.

patch.description:
* `expected_version` mismatch ⇒ `409 stale_project_version`.
* Unknown id ⇒ `404 project_not_found`.
* Per §9.2, `lead_user_id` mutation is an elevated op; v1
  handler does not yet enforce the elevation (a follow-up
  stage wires the lead-or-author check). The lane is reserved
  so adding the gate is a one-line edit.
* Audits [`audit::PROJECT_UPDATE`] after the row commits.

post.summary:
`POST /projects/{id}/adopt-milestone` — set or clear the
project's [`primary_milestone_id`](ProjectDto::primary_milestone_id).
Returns the updated [`ProjectDto`] so the caller can refresh
the `★ primary` chip without a follow-up GET.
post.description:
400 (`milestone_not_linked`) when the milestone exists but
doesn't belong to a repo currently linked to this project — the
strip never surfaces these but a stale UI must not be able to
adopt one via a direct API call.

400.description: Milestone not linked to this project's repos

post.summary:
`POST /projects/{id}/archive` — elevated archive op (§9.2).
Idempotent: archiving an already-archived row echoes it back
without bumping `version` or writing an audit row.

get.summary:
`GET /projects/{id}/board-links` — list the project's linked
boards, in `created_at ASC` order (so §6.3 renders a stable
sequence matching the operator's link-now order). Carries the
per-link `last_mirror_at` / `last_mirror_error` so the row can
render mirror status without a second round-trip.

post.summary:
`POST /projects/{id}/board-links` — link a board to the
project. The natural-key `(project_id, github_board_node_id)`
UNIQUE constraint surfaces a re-link of the same board as
`409 board_already_linked`. The picker-supplied cached
title / url ride through so the link row renders the right
name immediately. Audits [`audit::PROJECT_BOARD_LINK`].

delete.summary:
`DELETE /projects/{id}/board-links/{link_id}` — unlink a board
from the project. §9.2 elevation: caller must be the project's
`created_by`, its `lead_user_id`, or hold the `(projects,
admin)` lane. We approximate the admin lane here by checking
for the lead / author seat; further admin elevation rides on
top of the `(projects, write)` outer gate. The mirror items
(`dp_project_board_items`) cascade via `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
Audits [`audit::PROJECT_BOARD_UNLINK`].

403.description: Caller is not the project creator / lead

404.description: No such project, or link does not belong to it

get.summary:
`GET /projects/{id}/group-by-options` — dynamic dim list for
the Group-by dropdown (PROJECT-VIEW.md §7.3).
get.description:
Slice 2: `status` is the only fixed dim; every distinct
`dp_tags.key` linked to one of the project's issues (non-
archived, `kind='kv'`) becomes a `tag:<key>` entry. Cache /
invalidation per §7.3 is deferred — the query is cheap enough
on the slice-A target (≤100 issues per project) to run inline.

get.summary:
`GET /projects/{id}/issues` — paginated issue list scoped to a
project (§7.2). Same envelope as `GET /issues`.
get.description:
Implementation note: v1 resolves membership via
[`Store::list_issue_ids_for_project`], fetches each issue row
with [`Store::get_issue`], applies optional `state` / `q` filters
in-memory, then paginates. Correct for the slice-A target of
projects with ≤ 100 issues. The natural follow-up — a SQL-level
"filter `dp_issues` by `project_id`" — is deferred until
`IssueListFilter` grows a `project_id` field in slice B.

200.description: Paginated issue list scoped to the project

post.summary:
`POST /projects/{id}/issues` — bulk add (§7.2). Returns
`BulkAddResult` so per-row outcomes flow back in one round-trip.
post.description:
* `issue_ids` capped at [`BULK_ADD_ISSUE_CAP`]; over the cap
  returns `400 bulk_add_too_large`.
* CAS-gated on the project's `version`; mismatch returns
  `409 stale_project_version`.
* One audit row per accepted issue
  ([`audit::PROJECT_ISSUE_ADD`]); skipped rows never audit.

200.description: Per-row outcome of the bulk add

delete.summary:
`DELETE /projects/{id}/issues/{issue_id}?expected_version=` —
single detach (§7.2). 204 on success; CAS-gated on the project's
`version`. A no-op detach (the issue is not currently in this
project) is `404 project_issue_not_found` — same idempotence-at-
the-application-boundary contract as the store layer.

404.description: No such project, or issue is not in this project

get.summary:
`GET /projects/{id}/milestones` — milestones across every linked
repo, sorted by `(state ASC, due_on ASC NULLS LAST, title ASC)`
so the soonest-due open milestone is first and the no-due-date
tail sinks to the bottom of the open block.

parameters.name: include_closed
parameters.description:
When `true`, include `state = 'closed'` rows after the open
set (for the `▸ Show closed` toggle). Defaults to `false`.

post.summary:
`POST /projects/{id}/milestones` — create a milestone on a
linked repo and mirror it into `dp_milestones`.
post.description:
1. Resolve the project; 404 if missing.
2. Confirm `repo_id` is currently linked to this project; 400
   `repo_not_linked` otherwise (so a stale UI can't create
   milestones on arbitrary repos by id).
3. Resolve repo → org for the install-permission check.
4. [`require_issues_write`] gate; failure ⇒
   `403 writes_not_available_for_org`.
5. Call GitHub via [`MilestoneWriteBackend::create_milestone`].
6. Parse the response with [`parse_milestone_upsert`] and
   [`Store::upsert_milestone`] the row so the strip refreshes
   immediately.
7. Audit `project.milestone.create` with target
   `<project_id>:<repo_id>#<github_number>`.

200.description: Milestone created on GitHub and mirrored

400.description: Validation failed at GitHub, or repo not linked

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

delete.summary:
`DELETE /projects/{id}/milestones/{milestone_id}` — delete a
milestone from GitHub and from the local mirror.
delete.description:
Hard delete on both sides. `dp_projects.primary_milestone_id`
pointers clear via the FK's `ON DELETE SET NULL` (migration
0035). The handler returns 204 on success.

204.description: Milestone deleted on GitHub and locally

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

patch.summary:
`PATCH /projects/{id}/milestones/{milestone_id}` — edit a
mirrored milestone on GitHub and refresh the local row.
patch.description:
The `state` field doubles as the close/reopen verb: setting
it to `"closed"` audits as `project.milestone.close`,
`"open"` as `project.milestone.reopen`. Any other field
change audits as `project.milestone.update`. When `state` is
the only field set the handler still re-upserts the local
mirror from GitHub's response so `closed_at` lands in the
same tick.

200.description: Milestone updated on GitHub and mirrored

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

get.summary:
`GET /projects/{id}/repos` — list repos associated with the
project, in `added_at ASC` order.

put.summary:
`PUT /projects/{id}/repos/{repo_id}` — idempotently associate a
repo with the project. Enforces that the repo's `org_id` matches
the project's `org_id` (v1: one org per project, §4).

delete.summary:
`DELETE /projects/{id}/repos/{repo_id}` — remove the
association. Idempotent (a no-op delete returns 204).

get.summary:
`GET /projects/{id}/views` — caller's saved views in
`position ASC` order.

post.summary: `POST /projects/{id}/views` — create + append.
`POST /projects/{id}/views/reorder` — atomic position rewrite.

400.description: `ordered_ids` did not match the caller's view set

get.summary: `GET /projects/{id}/views/{view_id}`.

`GET /reports/freshness` — the data-freshness probe. Returns the
same envelope as the report routes but with `rows: null` so the
UI's "data as of …" widget can poll a single endpoint without
paying for an event scan.
get.description:
The resolved window is still echoed back (defaulting to
`last_7_days` UTC) so the response shape is uniform.

get.summary:
`GET /reports/home-org-split` — the SCOPE §7 cross-org executive
view. Always uses the [`ScopeMode::PerOrgSplit`] lens regardless
of what the request says (the route only makes sense in that
mode); each output row is one `(user, org)` bucket with the
count of distinct events the user is credited on in that org.

`GET /reports/issues` — §5.10 aggregate metrics over
`dp_issues`. Authorisation: `("issues", "read")`. The filter
scope is intersected with the caller's `org_ids` at the
handler boundary.

`GET /reports/org/:org_id` — counts for one org. The path
`:org_id` is forced into `request.orgs` (single-element) so the
`single_org` lens has the org to filter on regardless of what
the query string carried.

200.description: Counts for the org in the requested lens

post.summary: `POST /reports/project-portfolio`.
post.description:
Returns one row per visible project plus portfolio-level KPIs. The
envelope is a structured JSON body (not query string) because the
request carries an optional `window` object — same reason
SCOPE.md §15.6 chose POST for the activity-report envelope.

Visibility: trusts the caller-supplied `orgs` list, gated by the
outer `with_permission("reports", "read")` layer. A stricter
"orgs the caller can see" filter is an authz follow-up tracked
in PORTFOLIO-REPORT-PROGRESS.md.

200.description: One row per visible project + portfolio KPIs (ProjectPortfolioResponse)

get.summary:
`GET /reports/team/:team_id` — counts narrowed to one team
(passed through to the store via `request.teams`). Per-team
`group_by=team` is rejected in this stage; the route still
supports the other group-bys.

200.description: Counts for the team in the requested lens

get.summary:
`GET /reports/user/:user_id` — counts for one user across the
requested orgs / window / roles. The path `:user_id` is pushed
onto `request.users` so the query string can omit it (the path
is authoritative).

200.description: Counts for the user in the requested lens

get.summary:
`GET /repos` — paginated repo list with open-issue counts. Reads
only; not audited (low-sensitivity directory traversal, same
rationale as `GET /users` in [`crate::directory`]).

`GET /repos/{id}/activity-heatmap` — repo-level activity
`(day_of_week, hour_of_day)` distribution.
Authorisation: `("repos", "read")`.

`GET /repos/{id}/ci-stats` — repo-level CI workflow-run
statistics. Authorisation: `("repos", "read")`.

`GET /repos/{id}/contributor-diversity` — repo-level
"bus factor" view. Authorisation: `("repos", "read")`.

`GET /repos/{id}/metadata` — repo snapshot for the
repo-activity dashboard. Authorisation: `("repos", "read")`.

404.description: No such repo, or no snapshot recorded yet

get.summary:
`GET /repos/{id}/pr-size-stats` — repo-level PR-size
distribution. Authorisation: `("repos", "read")`.

`GET /repos/{id}/review-velocity` — repo-level time-to-merge
percentile distribution. Authorisation: `("repos", "read")`.

post.summary:
`POST /repos/{id}/sync` — operator-triggered per-repo
reconciler tick. Idempotent: if the scheduler is already
running a tick the call coalesces and the body is still
`{ "queued": true }` (the user's *intent* is queued even if
the scheduler decided to coalesce against an in-flight run).
Authorisation: `("repos", "sync")` — the one new auth pair in
slice 2.

503.description: Reconciler scheduler not configured in this deployment

get.summary:
`GET /repos/{id}/sync-status` — sync freshness badge data.
Authorisation: `("repos", "read")`.

`GET /repos/{repo_id}/issues/{number}` — single issue via the
canonical deep-link shape audit log entries already record.

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description: Include archived tags in the response. Default `false`.

200.description: Visible tags with viewer-filtered link counts

post.summary: `POST /tags` — create a tag.
post.description:
* Caller must be a scope member of the requested scope, else
  `403 tag_scope_member_required`.
* Case-insensitive name uniqueness per scope is a DB-level
  expression index — a clash surfaces as
  `409 tag_name_conflict`.
* Audit: writes [`audit::TAG_CREATE`] with target
  `"<scope_kind>:<scope_id>:<tag_id>"`.

403.description: Caller is not a member of the requested scope

409.description: Tag name already in use for this scope

get.summary: `GET /tags/{id}` — single tag, plus a page of its visible links.

404.description: Tag does not exist or is invisible to caller

patch.summary:
`PATCH /tags/{id}` — rename / recolour / set description /
archive. Mutually-exclusive verb mapping:
patch.description:
* If `archived` is set: emits [`audit::TAG_ARCHIVE`] (regardless
  of whether other fields are also patched in the same request).
* Otherwise emits [`audit::TAG_UPDATE`].

The two-verb split lets the audit log answer "when did this
tag retire?" with one query (`WHERE action = 'tag.archive'
AND target LIKE '<tag_id>'`) without scanning every
`tag.update` row.

403.description: Caller is not a scope member

404.description: Tag does not exist or is invisible

409.description: Tag name not unique within scope

post.summary:
`POST /tags/{id}/links` — batch link, transactional all-or-
nothing per §7.5.
post.description:
Per-item validation (pre-commit):
* `target_id` must not duplicate an existing link of the same
  `kind` on this tag (`duplicate`).
* `target_id` must not duplicate another row in the same
  batch (`duplicate_in_batch`).

On any per-item failure the response is `422 batch_rejected`
with an `items: [{index, code, message}, ...]` array and
**nothing is committed**. On success, one audit row per link
is written per §7.6, and `LinkBatchResponse.warning` is set
when the post-commit link count exceeds
[`TAG_LINK_WARN_THRESHOLD`] (§13.5).

403.description: Caller is not a scope member

404.description: Tag does not exist or is invisible

delete.description:
Same per-item error surface as link: items that do not match
a live `(kind, target_id)` on the tag come back as
`code = "not_linked"` and the whole batch is rejected (no
partial unlinks). One `tag.unlink` audit row per detached
link.

403.description: Caller is not a scope member

404.description: Tag does not exist or is invisible

get.summary: `GET /teams?org_id=…` — teams inside one org.
`GET /users` — list users, optionally filtered to one org.
get.description:
Audit: writes one `report.read`-style row… actually `directory`
reads aren't in the v1 audit vocabulary (D4.4 only pins the eight
listed verbs). Listing users is a low-sensitivity read so we
intentionally do not audit it. The stage-4 mutation that does
audit is `POST /home-org`.

post.summary: Documentation-only stub for `POST /webhooks/github`.
post.description:
The live receiver is `dp_fetcher::webhook::router::receive`;
authentication is the GitHub HMAC (`X-Hub-Signature-256`),
**not** a principal cookie. Stage 6 mirrors the route's
behaviour into the OpenAPI document so MCP / frontend clients
know it exists, without coupling `dp-fetcher` to utoipa.

This function is never invoked — `dp-server` mounts the real
router from `dp-fetcher` directly.

parameters.name: X-GitHub-Delivery
parameters.description: GitHub-issued delivery id; the inbox dedup key.

parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
parameters.description: Hex-encoded `sha256=<digest>` HMAC over the raw body.

200.description: Delivery enqueued (or replayed — GitHub retries on any non-2xx)

400.description: Missing required header or unparseable JSON body

500.description: Persistence failure other than a replay conflict

Ack.description:
Trivial response shape — handlers that don't return data still
return a body so the UI doesn't switch on `204`.

AddPinRequest.description:
Body for `POST /me/pins`. The server picks the position
(`len(existing)`) and the `pinned_at` timestamp.

AdoptMilestoneBody.description:
Body for [`adopt_milestone`]. `milestone_id = None` clears the
project's primary pointer; `Some(id)` adopts that milestone.

milestone_id.description: Milestone to adopt, or `null` to clear the pointer.

AppInstallBannerOrgDto.description:
One row in `GET /me/app-install-banner`.

`writes_available` mirrors the write-gate verdict for the
`(viewer, org)` pair so the frontend can render the §8.4
affordance without re-querying. `admin_copy_text` is the
§13.6 copy-able snippet; `manage_url` is the GitHub deep-link
(omitted when no App slug is configured).

admin_copy_text.description:
Copy-able admin text the viewer pastes into Slack / email
to ask their org admin to re-consent. Always present —
even for orgs where writes are already available, the
frontend hides the row but the text is harmless to carry.

manage_url.description:
GitHub-side deep-link to the install's permissions page.
`None` when no slug is configured or when no install
record exists for the org.

writes_available.description:
`true` iff a §8 issue write against this org would succeed
(deployment flag on AND install record allows
`issues: write`).

AppInstallBannerResponse.description:
Full §13.6 banner response.

`request_issues_write` mirrors the deployment-level flag so the
UI can render the "writes disabled in this deployment" mode
without inspecting each row's `writes_available`.

orgs.description:
One row per org the viewer is a member of (read through
`Store::list_memberships_for_user`). Orgs the viewer
cannot see at all are *not* included — the §15.11 access
gate is the single visibility check (§9 cross-ref).

request_issues_write.description:
`false` when [`GitHubAppConfig::request_issues_write`] is
off; the §8 surface is hard-disabled deployment-wide.

AppManifest.description:
The App's default permission set as declared in its manifest.

Each key is a GitHub permission resource (e.g. `"issues"`,
`"metadata"`); each value is the requested level (`"read"` or
`"write"`). [`app_manifest_permissions`] renders this from
[`GitHubAppConfig`] — `issues` is `"write"` when
[`GitHubAppConfig::request_issues_write`] is `true`, omitted
otherwise. The other resources are the read-only set the v1
reporting surface needs and do not change with the flag.

Used by deployment tooling and the (future) `/admin/app-manifest`
surface. Pure value; no side-effects.

default_permissions.description:
`resource -> level` map. Serialised in BTreeMap order so
the JSON is deterministic across runs (the OpenAPI
snapshot test cares).

slug.description:
App slug — informational, copied verbatim from
[`GitHubAppConfig::slug`]. Empty when unset.

ArchiveProjectRequest.description:
Body for `POST /projects/{id}/archive`. CAS-gated on the
project's current `version` (§9.2). The handler is idempotent —
archiving an already-archived project echoes the row back
without bumping `version`.

BoardLinkDto.description:
Wire form of [`BoardLink`] for the §7.3 GET / POST responses.
Carries the per-link `last_mirror_at` / `last_mirror_error`
aggregate columns the §6.3 row renders as
`Last sync: 14:23:07 ✓` / `Last sync: failed — …`.

github_board_cached_at.description: Wall-clock the cache was last refreshed.

github_board_node_id.description: GitHub Projects v2 board node id (`PVT_…`).

github_board_title.description:
Cached board title. `None` until the picker has refreshed
— the UI falls back to "Untitled board" in that case.

id.description:
Primary key — opaque to clients. The §7.3 DELETE handler
takes this in the URL so the wire shape never carries a
raw GitHub node id.

last_mirror_at.description:
Aggregate timestamp of the most recent successful mirror
across any item under this link. `None` until the first
success.

last_mirror_error.description:
Aggregate error from the most recent failed mirror across
any item under this link; `None` when the most recent
outcome was a success.

start_field_node_id.description:
Mapped start-date field, or `None` when the board has no
start field (mirror skips the lane).

updated_at.description: Last accepted mutation on the row.

date_fields.description:
Date-typed fields the mirror can write. Filtered server-
side so the dialog's `Start → / Due →` dropdowns only see
fields the mirror will accept.

node_id.description: GitHub Projects v2 board node id (`PVT_…`).

number.description:
Project number (`#12` etc.). Optional so a future
transport that doesn't surface it doesn't break the DTO.

url.description:
Deep link to github.com for this board, when GitHub
surfaces one. The §6.4 dialog uses this for the
`[Open GitHub project settings]` fallback when the picker
renders a single result and the user wants to inspect it
before linking.

BulkAddIssuesRequest.description:
Body for `POST /projects/{id}/issues`. CAS-gated on the project's
current `version` (§7.2); `issue_ids` is capped at
[`BULK_ADD_ISSUE_CAP`].

expected_version.description:
The `version` the caller observed on the project row. A
mismatch returns `409 stale_project_version` just like the
§7.1 PATCH / archive routes. Optional only when `view_id`
is set — view-scoped adds don't mutate the project row and
therefore don't need CAS. Required for project-level adds;
the handler returns `400 missing_expected_version` if it's
missing in that case.

issue_ids.description:
Issue ids to attach. Capped at [`BULK_ADD_ISSUE_CAP`]; over
the cap returns `400 bulk_add_too_large`. An empty array is
accepted as a no-op (returns `BulkAddResult { added: [],
skipped: [] }` and does not bump the project version).

view_id.description:
Optional saved-view id (PROJECT-VIEW.md §5.4 amendment).
When set, the accepted issues are *also* attached to the
named view's membership table after the project add
succeeds, so the tab the user added them on retains them.
Skipped (already-in-project) ids are still added to the
view — the user expects the issues to appear on the tab
regardless of whether they were brand new to the project.

BulkAddResult.description:
`BulkAddResult` — the per-row outcome shape `linear-projects-v2.md`
§7.2 / `SCOPE-PROJECTS.md` §7 wire through the REST layer so the
UI can render add-by-add status from one round-trip.

added.description: Issue ids the store accepted into the project.

skipped.description:
Issue ids the store refused, each with a closed-vocabulary
`reason`. See [`BulkAddSkipDto`].

BulkAddSkipDto.description:
One row in [`BulkAddResult::skipped`]. Mirrors
[`ProjectIssueAddSkip`] but kept as a separate wire type so the
OpenAPI schema is decoupled from the domain crate and so the
`reason` vocabulary is documented at the REST boundary.

existing_project_id.description:
Set when `reason == "already_in_project"`. Lets the UI link
directly to the existing project's detail page.

issue_id.description: The issue id that was rejected.

reason.description:
Closed-vocabulary reason; one of:

* `"already_in_project"` — the v1 `UNIQUE (issue_id)`
  constraint fired. `existing_project_id` is set so the UI
  can render a `Move here?` affordance.
* `"unknown_issue"` — the issue id did not resolve in
  `dp_issues`.
* `"cross_org"` — the issue's `org_id` differs from the
  project's `org_id` (v1: one org per project, §4).

BulkInboxOp.description:
Operation kind for [`BulkInboxRequest`]. One of mark-seen, snooze,
done, or restore-to-inbox — the four bulk actions the workbench
exposes from the list header.

BulkInboxRequest.description:
Body for `POST /me/inbox/bulk`. One operation applied to a batch
of issue ids.

touched.description:
Number of `dp_user_issue_state` rows touched (inserted +
updated). For `mark_all_seen` this is the upsert count from
the underlying `mark_issues_seen` call and is reported as the
length of the request batch (the store does not surface the
row count for that path today).

CountRow.description:
One aggregated count row. The `key` is stringified so the same
shape works for UUID group-bys (`User`, `Team`, `Repo`, `Org`) and
time-bucket group-bys (`Day`, `Week`, `Month` — RFC3339 instants).

count.description: Event count attributed to this bucket.

key.description: The bucket key, formatted as a string.

CreateBoardLinkRequest.description:
Body for `POST /projects/{id}/board-links`. Carries the board
the operator picked from the §6.4 dialog plus the field-id
mappings the picker resolved. The cached `github_board_title`
/ `github_board_url` ride through too so the link row renders
the right name immediately, without a second picker round-trip.

github_board_node_id.description: GitHub board node id chosen from [`BoardPickerDto::node_id`].

github_board_title.description:
Picker-resolved title. Optional — the nightly refresh
backfills it if absent.

start_field_node_id.description:
Mapped start-date field. Omit when the board has no start
field — the mirror skips that lane.

CreateIssueRequest.description:
Body for `POST /issues`. The repo to mutate is named explicitly
(there is no canonical row yet to derive it from). The optional
`project_id` / `view_id` lanes let the handler attach the
freshly-created issue to a project (and optionally a saved
view tab) in the same request, mirroring the bulk-add
semantics in [`crate::project_issues::BulkAddIssuesRequest`].

expected_version.description:
CAS token — the project's observed `version`. Required
when `project_id` is set and `view_id` is unset (project-
level attach mutates the project row); ignored otherwise.

project_id.description:
Optional project id to attach the new issue to in the same
request. When set without `view_id`, the handler runs the
project-level add ("All" tab semantics) and requires
`expected_version`. When set together with `view_id`, the
handler attaches the issue only to the named view's
membership table and does not touch project membership.

repo_id.description: Internal repo id the new issue belongs to.

view_id.description:
Optional saved-view id (PROJECT-VIEW.md §5.4 amendment).
Requires `project_id`. Ignored when `project_id` is unset.

CreateIssueResponse.description:
Acknowledgement body for `POST /issues`. Returns the GitHub-side
number GitHub assigned (so the UI can deep-link immediately) and
echoes the actor's `repo_id` for symmetry with PATCH responses.
`issue_id` is populated when the local `dp_issues` row was
materialised synchronously from the GitHub create payload — the
UI can use it to render the new row in-list without waiting for
the next sync. It is `None` when the backend could not surface a
payload (the unconfigured stub, certain fakes), in which case
the row appears once the fetcher / webhook brings it down.

issue_id.description:
Local `dp_issues.id` when the row was materialised in this
request, otherwise `None`.

repo_id.description:
The repo to create the milestone in. Must be currently
linked to the project (via `dp_project_repos`); otherwise
the handler returns `400 repo_not_linked`.

CreateProjectRequest.description:
Body for `POST /projects`. `status` is optional — when omitted
the server defaults to [`ProjectStatusDto::Active`] (§6.2 "Status
defaults to `active`"). `created_by` is filled from the
[`Principal`], not the body.

CreateTagRequest.description:
Body for `POST /tags`. Server picks `id`, `created_by`,
`created_at`. `scope_id` is required; the caller must be a
scope member or the request returns `403`.

name.description:
Display name. Case-insensitive uniqueness is enforced per
scope by the migration-0005 expression index — a clash
surfaces as `409 tag_name_conflict`.

scope_id.description:
Owning user/team/org id. For `user`-scope tags, must equal
the caller (returns `403 tag_scope_member_required`
otherwise).

DataAsOfDto.description:
`data_as_of` wire shape. Mirrors `dp_domain::freshness::DataAsOf`
but with the serde derives + utoipa schema the dp-domain type
intentionally lacks (dp-domain stays free of HTTP-shape concerns
per §0.6).

headline.description:
Convenience headline picked by lens (SCOPE §11.7). `None`
for `per_org_split` (the UI renders per row) and for
`single_org` / `all_orgs_combined` when the requested orgs
have no freshness entry yet.

per_org.description:
Per-org reconciler freshness. Absent orgs have never been
touched by the reconciler (treat as "pending", not "stale").

DateFieldDto.description:
One date-typed field exposed in the picker. Carries the
GraphQL node id so the POST body can round-trip the operator's
choice without a second picker call.

name.description:
Field name as configured on the GitHub board
(e.g. `"Begin date"`, `"Target date"`).

ExportEvent.description:
Per-event projection inside the export. Carries the event row
plus every role this user played on it — a squash-merge author
who later closed the same PR shows up once with
`roles: ["author", "closer"]`.

event_id.description: Event id (the join key inside the export).

roles.description: Every role the exported user played on this event.

FetchRunDto.description:
Wire row for `GET /admin/runs`. Mirrors [`FetchRun`] with serde
derives + `ToSchema` so the openapi document picks it up.

error_sample.description:
Bounded sample of per-item failure context, captured by the
fetcher so the admin UI can explain *why* `errors > 0`
without leaving the page. `None` for clean runs and for
runs that pre-date the column.

errors.description: Items that errored during the run.

finished.description: Wall-clock end (UTC). `None` while the run is in flight.

partial.description: `true` if the run finished but some items failed.

FetchRunErrorSampleDto.description:
One captured failure inside a [`FetchRunDto`]. Mirrors
[`FetchRunErrorSample`] verbatim so the wire shape matches
the domain shape — only added so `ToSchema` shows it in the
openapi document.

org.description: Org login at the time of capture.

repo.description: `owner/name` of the repo, when the failure was repo-scoped.

id.description:
Wire-form dim id passed back as `?group_by=<id>` — e.g.
`status`, `tag:gate`.

label.description:
Display label. For `tag:<key>` this is the key title-cased
in v1; richer labels (gate prefix, milestone titles) ride in
when the ordinal-taxonomy config lands (PROJECT-VIEW.md §10.1).

GroupByOptionsResponse.description:
Body for `GET /projects/{id}/group-by-options` — dynamic
dimension catalogue powering the Group-by dropdown
(PROJECT-VIEW.md §5.1 / §7.3).

dims.description:
Ordered list of dimensions the toolbar can show. `status`
is always present; one `tag:<key>` entry per distinct kv
key observable on the project's issues. Sticky keys from
saved views (§5.1) will be merged in when slice 4 lands.

HomeOrgSplitRow.description:
One row of the `/reports/home-org-split` shape — per (user, org)
bucket, count of distinct events the user is credited on within
that org.

InboxStatusDto.description:
Wire form of [`InboxStatus`]. Lower-case to match the SQL form
declared in migration 0011.

IssueBucket.description:
One bucket in [`IssueListResponse::buckets`]. The label is the
human-readable form the client renders verbatim; `key` is the
stable identifier used for collapse state and as the
`bucket_keys` value on `IssueDto`.

closed.description: Closed issue count in this bucket, post-filter.

key.description:
Stable bucket key (`g3-mvp-build`, `open`, `<uuid>` for
milestone/type buckets). `None` for the synthetic "No <key>"
bucket.

label.description:
Human-readable label (`G3 · MVP build`, `Open`). For now
equals `key` for tag buckets; richer labels (gate prefix,
milestone title) land with the ordinal-taxonomy config
(PROJECT-VIEW.md §5.1 / §10.1) and milestone joins.

open.description: Open issue count in this bucket, post-filter.

IssueDatesDto.description:
Response body — the canonical post-upsert row. Mirrors
[`IssueDates`] one-for-one so the UI can render the freshly
stamped `updated_at` plus the most recent mirror outcome
(`mirror_synced_at` / `mirror_error`) without a second read.

mirror_node_id.description:
Projects v2 item node id, when mirroring has ever
succeeded for this row.

mirror_synced_at.description:
Wall-clock the most recent mirror attempt succeeded;
`null` until the first success.

IssueDto.description:
Full issue projection. Matches the shape the frontend's
`IssueDto` already declared (`api/client.ts`) so the existing
§8.3 detail pane wires up without DTO shape changes.

bucket_keys.description:
Bucket keys assigned by an active `group_by` (PROJECT-VIEW.md
§7.2). Populated **only** by `GET /projects/{id}/issues` when
`?group_by=` is set. Each entry is the bucket the issue
belongs to — `None` (serialised as `null`) for the synthetic
"No <key>" bucket. An issue can appear in multiple buckets
when `group_by=tag:<key>` and the issue carries multiple kv
values for the same key (e.g. `category:firmware` +
`category:hardware`). Omitted entirely when no grouping is
active.

repo_slug.description:
Short `owner/repo` label rendered in list rows. Populated
by a per-page join through `repo_id -> (org_login, name)`.
Omitted when the join is unavailable (point-lookup detail
handlers backfill this too so the peek panel and the row
it was selected from agree).

tags.description:
DP tags currently attached to this issue, filtered to the
viewer-visible subset per tagging.md §7.4. Populated by the
list and detail handlers; absent (treated as empty by
clients) on responses built before that join lands. Each
entry is the slim chip-render projection (`id`, `name`,
`color`, `scope_kind`) — enough for the issue-detail
picker and the row chips, no per-link metadata.

unread.description:
Per-caller unread flag — `true` when the issue's `version`
is newer than what the caller has marked seen. Only the
`/me/queue` endpoint populates this with a meaningful value;
every other endpoint emits `false`. Defaults to `false` so
older frontend clients that ignore the field render rows
the same as before.

buckets.description:
Server-side bucket sidecar — populated **only** by
`GET /projects/{id}/issues` when `?group_by=` is set
(PROJECT-VIEW.md §7.2). Counts are **post-filter** (§5.2)
and authoritative; the client never re-buckets. `key` is
`None` for the synthetic "No <key>" bucket. Bucket ordering
is server-decided (§5.1 — ordinal taxonomies first, then
count desc).

total.description: Total matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

IssuePatch.description:
Field-level patch the PATCH handler forwards to GitHub. Every
field is optional — only `Some(_)` lanes are sent to GitHub. The
caller is the source of truth on what to mutate; the handler
performs no field-vs-field consistency checks.

assignees.description:
Replacement assignee logins. `None` leaves assignees
untouched.

body.description: New body (omitted when not changing; explicit `null` clears).

labels.description: Replacement label list. `None` leaves labels untouched.

state.description:
New state — `"open"` or `"closed"`. The handler routes this
to the `issue.close` / `issue.reopen` audit verbs.

IssueStateDto.description:
Wire form of [`IssueState`]. Lower-case to match GitHub's wire
form (`"open"` / `"closed"`).

IssueTagDto.description:
Slim per-issue tag chip projection embedded in [`IssueDto::tags`].
Tracks just what the workflow UI needs to render a chip and let
the user remove it (`tag_id` keys the `DELETE /tags/{id}/links`
call). Visibility is the *tag*'s — issue visibility is enforced
by the parent handler.

color.description: Hex colour token used by the chip renderer.

id.description: Tag id (the picker uses this for link/unlink).

scope_kind.description:
`user` / `team` / `org`. Lets the UI surface "your tag" vs
"team tag" without a second round-trip.

rows.description: Bucketed rows, sorted by bucket asc.

bucket.description: Bucket label (repo id, org id, assignee login, or ISO date).

count.description: Row count contributing to the value (useful for medians).

value.description:
Metric value — count for throughput/wip/stale/untriaged,
median seconds for lead_time.

items.description:
Items to link. Transactional all-or-nothing; per-item
errors are returned via [`ApiError::Batch`] on rejection.

LinkBatchResponse.description:
Response from `POST /tags/{id}/links` on success — the
attached link rows plus an optional soft warning when the
tag's link count crosses [`TAG_LINK_WARN_THRESHOLD`] (§13.5).

linked.description: The persisted link rows in insertion order.

warning.description:
Optional advisory warning. `"tag_link_count_high"` when
the tag now holds more than the warning threshold — the
operation committed regardless (§13.5 "the response
carries the warning, the operation still commits").

LinkRequestItem.description:
One entry in a `POST /tags/{id}/links` request — what to
attach.

MarkSeenRequest.description:
Body for `POST /me/inbox/seen`. The server marks every listed
issue as read up to its current `version`. Empty list is a
no-op (`204`). Capped at 200 ids per request to keep the
SQL bind size sane — clients with more than that should
page their reads via the list endpoint anyway.

MeIdentitiesResponse.description:
Top-level response. JSON object (not bare list) so additive
fields like `principal_dirty` / pagination metadata can land
without a breaking change.

identities.description:
The viewer's linked identities, ordered by `linked_at`
**descending** (newest first — the §10 page renders the
primary at the top of the stack).

primary_id.description:
The `id` of the row marked `is_primary == true`, or `None`
if the viewer has no linked identities (i.e. local-password
only). The SPA reads this instead of re-scanning the list.

MeIdentityDto.description:
One linked identity in the response. `id` is a synthetic
stable handle the SPA can key on — it is `"{provider}:{sub}"`
rather than the bare `provider_sub` so two rows from different
providers can never collide and so the SPA never has to assume
a specific provider's sub format.

display_name.description:
Display name the provider returned at link / last sign-in.
Often the GitHub login or the Google given-name — the wire
shape is provider-defined.

email.description: Email the provider returned at link / last sign-in.

id.description:
Synthetic stable id: `"{provider}:{provider_sub}"`. Safe to
expose because the SPA already sees `provider`, and
`provider_sub` for the *currently signed-in* identity is
already in the OAuth callback URL flow — wrapping it in a
composite `id` keys React renders without inviting the SPA
to parse the sub out by itself.

is_primary.description:
`true` for the row currently treated as the primary
identity (the most-recent `linked_at`, matching
[`starter_auth_oauth::OAuthPrincipalExtras`]).

linked_at.description:
Wall-clock time the identity was first linked. v1 doubles
as "last login" because `IdentityStore` does not yet touch
the row on sign-in; the contract here is the same as
`starter_auth_oauth::IdentitySummary`'s `last_login_at`.

joined_at.description: When dev-pulse first observed this membership.

MilestoneDto.description:
One milestone row on the wire. The strip needs every
progress-bar field — `open_issues`, `closed_issues`,
`due_on` — plus the `repo_id` so the chip can disambiguate
when two repos share a milestone title.

github_number.description:
GitHub-side milestone number (the integer in the
`https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/milestone/{n}` URL).

repo_id.description:
Parent repo. The strip uses this for the
disambiguation suffix when two linked repos share a
milestone title.

OrgProjectPickerDto.description:
`GET /orgs/{org_id}/projects-v2` response (§7.3). Normalized so
the REST contract never leaks the GraphQL envelope. The
`fetched_at` field is stamped server-side at picker run so the
UI can render the freshness explicitly when an operator
re-opens the dialog (the picker itself is a cache-by-default
read but rebuilds the cache on every call — see
[`crate::state::AppState`] notes on the picker backend).

boards.description:
Boards visible to the deployment, in GitHub-provided order
(typically most-recently-touched first). Closed boards are
filtered out by the normaliser so only link-able targets
appear in the dialog.

fetched_at.description:
Wall-clock the picker ran. Lets the UI render
`Fetched 14:23:07` next to the dropdown.

PatchIssueDatesRequest.description:
Body for `PATCH /issues/{id}/dates`. Both fields are optional —
`null` (or omitted) clears that side. The schema CHECK guards
`start_at <= due_at`; the handler surfaces violations as
`400 invalid_date_window`.

due_at.description: New due instant (inclusive). Omit / `null` to clear.

start_at.description: New start instant (inclusive). Omit / `null` to clear.

expected_version.description:
CAS token — the `dp_issues.version` the UI rendered the form
against. The §18.2 step 5 CAS misses if this is stale, and
the handler returns `409 stale_local_version`.

PatchMilestoneRequest.description:
Body for [`patch_project_milestone`]. Mirrors the
`Option<Option<_>>` shape of [`MilestonePatchInput`] on the
wire so callers can distinguish "leave as-is" (omit the key)
from "clear" (send `null`).

Serde's `#[serde(default, deserialize_with = …)]` with
`serde_with::rust::double_option` would be the canonical
implementation; we inline a small helper instead to avoid
pulling in a dependency for one struct.

description.description:
Description. Omit to leave as-is; `null` to clear; string
to replace.

due_on.description:
Due date. Omit / `null` / value — same tri-state as
`description`.

title.description: New title. Omit to leave as-is.

PatchProjectRequest.description:
Body for `PATCH /projects/{id}`. Carries the §8.2
`expected_version` plus the merged-in field set. Fields that
are omitted are left untouched — the store layer takes a full
upsert payload, so the handler reads the current row and
overlays the partial body. This keeps the wire shape narrow
without leaking the upsert's "all fields required" shape.

description.description:
New description; pass `null` explicitly to clear by sending
`{"description": null}` (we cannot distinguish that from
"missing" with `#[serde(default)]`, so today the only way
to clear is via PATCH with `description: null` interpreted
in the handler — see [`patch_project`]).

expected_version.description:
The `version` the caller observed; the server CASes against
this and surfaces a `stale_project_version` 409 on mismatch.

lead_user_id.description:
New lead. `None` ⇒ leave unchanged. `Some(None)` ⇒ clear.
Mutating this is an elevated op per §9.2; v1 handler does
not yet check the elevation but the lane is wired so the
follow-up that ships lead-or-author resolution can land
the check without a wire change.

PercentileTripleDto.description:
p50 / p90 / p95 over a numeric distribution. Every field is
`null` when the sample is too small (SCOPE §15.9, `n < 5`); the
`sample_n` on the parent response carries the actual count so
the UI can render "n too small" instead of zeros.

PinDto.description:
One row in `GET /me/pins`. Hydration of `target_id` to a full
repo / tag payload is a follow-up stage — for now the client
joins against `/orgs`, `/repos`, `/tags` itself.

position.description: Sidebar order. Lower comes first; assigned by the server.

PinKindDto.description:
Wire form of [`PinKind`]. Mirrors the lower-case strings in the
`dp_user_pins.kind` CHECK constraint (`'repo' | 'tag'`).

ProjectDto.description:
One row of `GET /projects` and the body shape for the
single-row endpoints. Mirrors `linear-projects-v2.md` §7.1.

board_link_count.description:
Count of `dp_project_board_links` rows attached to this
project. Slice A returns `0` (the link table lands in
slice B); the DTO carries the field now so clients can
rely on a stable shape.

closed_issue_count.description:
Denormalised count of attached issues whose `dp_issues.state
= 'closed'`. Drives the §6.2 progress bar.

created_by.description:
Author (`dp_users.id`). Immutable per §9.2. `None` when the
original author was pseudonymised.

due_at.description: Planned due instant, UTC. `None` when unset.

lead_user_id.description:
Lead user. Drives default visibility and `Mentioned` filter
targets. Mutating this field is an elevated op (§9.2).

name.description:
Project name (case-insensitively unique within org for
non-archived rows, §8 partial index).

primary_milestone_id.description:
Adopted primary milestone (PROJECT-VIEW.md §5.5 / §9.5).
Set / cleared by `POST /projects/{id}/adopt-milestone`.

start_at.description: Planned start instant, UTC. `None` when unset.

version.description:
§8.2 CAS counter. PATCH / archive callers echo this back
as `expected_version`; a mismatch ⇒ 409 conflict.

ProjectListResponse.description:
Paginated envelope mirroring [`crate::issues_read::IssueListResponse`].
`rows` is omitted when the caller passes `?count_only=1` and the
envelope collapses to `{ total, limit, offset, rows: [] }` — the
sidebar (§6.1) uses this to render counts without dragging the
full row payload over the wire.

rows.description: Projects on this page, ordered per §6.2 (status → due → name).

total.description: Total matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

ProjectRepoDto.description:
One row in [`list_project_repos`]'s response. Enriched with the
repo's `org_id` and `name` so the §6.3 UI does not have to fan
out a `GET /repos/{id}` per row.

added_by.description: User who created the association, if known.

project_id.description: The project this row associates the repo with.

repo_org_login.description:
Enriched repo org login — used by the frontend to build
`https://github.com/{org_login}/{repo_name}` links.

ProjectStatusDto.description:
Wire form of [`ProjectStatus`]. Lowercase to mirror the SQL
CHECK vocabulary and the §6.1 sidebar labels.

ProjectViewCreateBody.description:
`POST /projects/{id}/views` body. Identical to PATCH apart from
being required (POST has no partial-update semantics).

due_date.description:
Optional due date for the view's timeline. Same shape as
[`Self::start_date`].

filter_clauses.description:
Canonical filter clauses; validated against
[`ProjectViewFilterClause`] before insert.

group_by.description:
Group-by dimension, or `null` for a flat view. `"status"`
or `"tag:<key>"`.

sort.description:
Sort order. Empty string is rejected — the client sends
`"updated_desc"` to mean "default".

start_date.description:
Optional start date for the view's timeline (AU
`dd/mm/yyyy` in the picker, `YYYY-MM-DD` on the wire).

ProjectViewDto.description:
One saved view on the wire. The serialised shape of
`filter_clauses` is the discriminated `#[serde(tag = "dim")]`
enum mirrored in `dp_domain::project_view`.

due_date.description:
Optional due date for the view's timeline. Same shape as
[`Self::start_date`].

group_by.description: Group-by dimension or `null` for a flat view.

open_issue_count.description:
Open issues currently visible inside this view (post-filter,
post-membership). `None` on write responses where the count
would be a wasted round-trip — only `GET /projects/{id}/views`
populates it.

position.description: Per-owner position within the project's tab strip.

start_date.description:
Optional start date for the view's timeline.
Serialised as `YYYY-MM-DD` (or omitted/null when unset).

total_issue_count.description:
Total issues currently visible inside this view (open +
closed). Same population rule as [`Self::open_issue_count`].

ProjectViewReorderBody.description:
`POST /projects/{id}/views/reorder` body — the full ordered
id list for the caller's views on this project.

ordered_ids.description: New order. Must equal the caller's existing view-id set.

PutSettingRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /me/settings/{key}`. `value` is the plaintext
the user typed (for secret keys, this is the only ingress
path — the GET handlers never echo it back).

value.description:
New value for the setting. Empty string is accepted and
distinguishable from "no row" — pass `DELETE` to remove
the row entirely.

items.description: Total deliveries applied during the tick.

oneOf.description: The trigger coalesced into an in-flight tick.

RefreshResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /admin/refresh`. Variants are flattened
so a coalesce comes out as `{ "ran": false }` and a real tick
as `{ "ran": true, "items": …, "errors": …, "partial": … }`.

ReorderRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /me/pins/order`. The slice **must** exactly cover
the caller's current pin set — extra / missing entries are
rejected (`400 reorder_set_mismatch`).

order.description:
New order. Entry `i` becomes `position = i` after the
transaction commits.

RepoActivityHeatmapDto.description:
`GET /repos/{id}/activity-heatmap` response — dense 168-cell
`(dow, hour)` grid of activity events for the repo. Describes
the repo's collaboration cadence, never an individual's
(SCOPE §4).

timezone.description: Echoed IANA timezone used for bucketing.

total.description: Total events across all buckets in the window.

RepoCiStatsDto.description:
`GET /repos/{id}/ci-stats` response — repo-level CI
workflow-run health. Every field describes the repo's CI, not
an individual contributor (SCOPE §4).

duration_sample_n.description:
Runs whose payload carried both `run_started_at` and
`updated_at` and a strictly-positive delta.

duration_seconds.description:
p50 / p90 / p95 over `updated_at - run_started_at`, in
seconds. `null` triple when `duration_sample_n < 5`.

success_rate.description:
`success / (success + failure)` ∈ `[0.0, 1.0]`, or `null`
when there were no terminal success / failure runs.

total_runs.description: Total workflow runs in the window.

RepoContributorDiversityDto.description:
`GET /repos/{id}/contributor-diversity` response —
repo-level "bus factor" view. Every field describes the
repo's concentration risk, not an individual contributor
(SCOPE §4). The wire shape deliberately carries no user
identifiers.

sample_n.description: Total (merged-PR, author) pairs in the window.

top1_share.description:
Share of `sample_n` from the single top author, in
`[0.0, 1.0]`. `null` when `sample_n < 5`.

top3_share.description:
Share of `sample_n` from the top 3 authors combined.
`null` when `sample_n < 5`.

RepoListResponse.description:
Paginated envelope. Carries `total` so the UI can render
`Showing X–Y of Z` without a second round-trip.

limit.description: Echoed back so the client can confirm what it asked for.

offset.description: Echoed back so the client can confirm what it asked for.

total.description: Total matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

RepoMetadataDto.description:
`GET /repos/{id}/metadata` response — the per-repo snapshot of
mutable GitHub-side fields (stars / forks / language / default
branch / archival state, …) populated by the fetcher off every
webhook delivery's `repository` block.

All numeric fields default to `0`; nullable fields default to
`null`. The endpoint returns `404` when no snapshot row has been
recorded for the repo yet (fresh install before the first
webhook lands) — the UI shows a "snapshot pending" placeholder
rather than rendering zeros.

metadata_updated_at.description: Wall-clock the dev-pulse fetcher last refreshed this row.

open_issues_remote.description:
Open issues + PRs as GitHub itself counts them. Differs
from the dev-pulse `open_issue_count` (issues only) by the
number of open PRs.

primary_language.description: Primary language detected by GitHub, if any.

pushed_at.description: GitHub's `pushed_at` — last push to any branch.

RepoPrSizeStatsDto.description:
`GET /repos/{id}/pr-size-stats` response — repo-level
pull-request size distribution. Every field describes the
repo, never an individual contributor (SCOPE §4).

sample_n.description:
Number of merged PRs whose payload carried diff-size fields
inside the window.

RepoReviewVelocityDto.description:
`GET /repos/{id}/review-velocity` response — repo-level
time-to-merge percentile distribution. Every field describes
the repo's merge cadence, not an individual contributor's
(SCOPE §4).

sample_n.description:
Merged PRs in the window whose payload carried both
`created_at` and `merged_at` with a positive delta.

time_to_merge_seconds.description:
p50 / p90 / p95 over `merged_at - created_at`, in seconds.
`null` triple when `sample_n < 5`.

RepoSummaryDto.description:
Row in `GET /repos`. Carries the join from `dp_orgs` so callers
don't have to round-trip for `org_login`, plus the two counters
the workflow list pane renders inline.

last_activity_at.description:
Most recent issue `updated_at`; `null` if the repo has no
issues yet.

open_issue_count.description: Number of open issues in this repo.

RepoSyncQueuedDto.description:
Wire envelope for `POST /repos/{id}/sync`. Always
`{ "queued": true }` on the 202 reply.

RepoSyncStatusDto.description:
Wire envelope for `GET /repos/{id}/sync-status`. See
`linear-projects-idea.md` §5.9. `queued` is `false` for now;
the scheduler does not expose per-repo in-flight introspection
so the badge UX treats "queued" as a transient client-side
flag set after a successful POST.

last_attempt_at.description:
When the last attempt finished — same value as
`last_synced_at` until the migration grows an
`attempted_at` column.

last_error.description: Last error, or `null` if the latest sync succeeded.

last_synced_at.description: When the last successful sync landed.

queued.description:
`true` if the scheduler is in the middle of reconciling
this repo. Currently always `false` — see module comment.

ReportResponse.description:
The envelope every report handler returns. `rows` is left as
[`serde_json::Value`] so the same struct serves the five report
shapes without forcing a per-handler enum — the OpenAPI doc
describes each handler's `rows` schema via per-route `body =
<Concrete>` overrides (added when the aggregator lands).

empty_reason.description:
Why the report has no rows, when the emptiness is the
*intentional* SCOPE-PROJECTS §7.7 outcome of the tag filter
not matching the requested metric's attribution column
(e.g. an `issue`-only tag queried against a commit metric).

`None` for every other empty result (window too tight,
no matching events, etc.) — those stay as `rows: []` so the
UI's existing empty-state copy still renders. Locked literal
is [`EMPTY_REASON_TAG_KIND_MISMATCH`].

resolved_window.description:
The UTC window the report ran against. Echoed verbatim from
[`resolve_window`] so the UI can label the report without
re-resolving (§0.4).

org_id.description: Org that becomes the new home for that user.

user_id.description: User to flip home org for.

SetInboxStateRequest.description:
Body for `PATCH /me/inbox/{issue_id}`. Either field may be
absent; an empty body leaves the row untouched (still upserted
at default values if it did not exist).

Consistency between `status` and `snoozed_until` is the caller's
responsibility — the server does not refuse `status = Inbox`
with `snoozed_until = Some(_)` so the UI can clear the snooze
by setting the status alone without a second round-trip.

snoozed_until.description: New snooze deadline. Use explicit `null` to clear.

oneOf.description:
New status (defaults to existing value when absent — for a
fresh row this means [`InboxStatusDto::Inbox`]).

SettingDto.description:
One setting on the wire. `value` is `null` for unset keys
and for `is_secret` keys that have been set — the UI reads
`has_value` to render the "set" affordance.

has_value.description:
Whether a row exists for `(user, key)`. `true` for both
secret and non-secret keys when the user has set a value.

is_secret.description:
Whether the catalogue marks this key as a secret. The UI
uses this to pick `<input type="password">` vs plain text
and to render the redaction affordance.

updated_at.description: When the row was last written. `None` for unset keys.

value.description:
The actual value. `null` when the key is `is_secret` or
when no row exists. Non-secret keys with a row return the
plaintext here.

TagDetailResponse.description:
`GET /tags/{id}` response: the tag plus a *page* of its links
(§7.5: "links are paginated separately (`?links_page=…`) to
keep a single response bounded even for tags near the §13.5
500-link soft warning").

links.description: One page of links — only those visible to the viewer.

links_page.description: Zero-based page index of the returned slice.

TagDto.description:
Tag row carried back to the client. Mirrors [`Tag`] but the
three nullable `scope_*_id` columns are collapsed into a single
`scope_id` — the discriminator + id is enough on the wire, and
matches how the frontend renders it.

visible_link_count.description:
**Viewer-visible** link count — never the true total
(§7.4). Populated by every list / get path.

TagLinkDto.description:
One link row carried back to the client. Mirrors [`TagLink`]
but collapses the four `target_*_id` columns into a single
`target_id` paired with [`kind`](Self::kind).

target_id.description: Linked repo / issue / user / team id per [`kind`](Self::kind).

TagLinkKindDto.description: Wire form of [`TagLinkKind`] — `repo | issue | user | team`.

login.description: GitHub login the token belongs to.

name.description: Display name from the GitHub profile (may be `null`).

oneOf.description:
Token did not authenticate. `code` is one of
`unauthorized`, `rate_limited`, `network`, `unset`.

TestGithubPatResponse.description:
Response from the `github.pat` connectivity probe. Carries
either an `ok: true` payload with the GitHub identity the
token resolves to, or `ok: false` with a stable `code` the
UI can switch on.

TimelineEntryDto.description:
Wire form of an issue-timeline row. The shape mirrors §5.6 —
the peek panel renders this as a vertical activity strip.

total.description: Total matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

UnlinkBatchRequest.description:
Body for `DELETE /tags/{id}/links` — batch unlink. Same
`(kind, target_id)` shape as link — IDs are resolved on the
server inside the same transaction so a partial unlink is
impossible.

UpdateTagRequest.description:
Body for `PATCH /tags/{id}`. Every field is optional; missing
fields are left unchanged. Setting `archived_at: Some(true)`
archives the tag (§7.4 — no hard delete); `Some(false)`
un-archives.

archived.description:
`Some(true)` archives, `Some(false)` un-archives, `None`
leaves the archive bit alone.

description.description:
Set or clear the description.
`None` leaves untouched; `Some(None)` clears.

github_id.description: GitHub numeric user id (stable across renames).

UserExport.description:
Top-level shape emitted by `GET /admin/users/:id/export`.
Documented for the openapi schema even though the response is
served as a chunked stream — the wire JSON parses to this type.

events.description: Every event this user is credited on, ordered by `ts ASC`.

user.description: The user row (already pseudonymised if previously deleted).

UserIssueStateDto.description:
One row in the inbox state table. Echoed back by the
PATCH handler so the UI can confirm the write without a
follow-up GET.

last_seen_version.description: Highest `dp_issues.version` the caller has marked seen.

snoozed_until.description: Wake-up instant for snoozed rows. `None` for inbox / done.
